```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(gatekeepR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Configuration is explicit and serializable. The example configuration is useful
for smoke tests and for learning the object shape.

```{r config}
cfg <- gk_example_config()
gk_validate_config(cfg)
gk_config_hash(cfg)
```

For a project configuration, declare the panel, signal policies, phenotype
hierarchy, and minimum support rules with `gk_panel()`, `gk_signal_policy()`,
`gk_hierarchy()`, and `gk_min_support()`. Validate it before preparing data:

```{r config-template, eval=FALSE}
cfg <- gk_config(
  panel = gk_panel(c("marker_a", "marker_b")),
  hierarchy = gk_hierarchy(...),
  signal_policy = gk_signal_policy(...),
  min_support = gk_min_support(...)
)
gk_validate_config(cfg)
gk_write_config(cfg, "config.json")
```

The configuration hash is recorded with prepared objects, reviews, and exports.
Changing a rule therefore creates a new computational identity instead of
silently changing an existing review.
